notes: Financial statement mapping: historical EBIT is treated as total operating income (operating income) from the consolidated statements (includes SAP S4 upgrade expense and impairments/other charges). ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

NWC construction (used for historical and as base-case % of sales): NWC = (Receivables + Inventories + Other current assets) - (Total current liabilities - Current maturities of long-term debt). This includes current operating lease liabilities as part of operating current liabilities by construction (definition choice). ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Base-case growth and margin trajectory is a modeling assumption intended to be consistent with management’s outlook that international activity is expected to be stable year-over-year (flat to modestly up) while North America is expected to decline year-over-year compared to 2025. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Tax rate: base-case tax_rate uses a normalized level derived from the company’s reported effective tax rates (2023-2025) with caution that 2025 is affected by impairments/valuation allowance changes. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

NOL fields: set nol_balance and nol_utilization_pct to null because the 10-K provides tax-effected deferred tax asset information and NOL-related realizability context, but does not provide a remaining NOL balance in a directly usable “tax attribute dollars” form for modeling. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Investments: set investments to null because the 10-K cash flow discloses purchases/sales of investment securities and equity investments, but a clean “investment balance sheet adjustment” breakout suitable for DCF net debt/capitalization purposes is not provided in a way that can be mapped to this specific field without additional modeling conventions. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Comps: peer multiples come from a secondary comp snapshot table (NTM snapshot; Nov 2025) and should be refreshed with a live data provider for execution-grade valuation work. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

Terminal assumptions: terminal_exit_ebitda_multiple and terminal method (average) are judgmental and anchored to the peer EV/NTM EBITDA context; bulls/bears adjust only terminal valuation parameters alongside WACC and normalization pace. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

catalysts: North America utilization/market conditions improving enough to lift stimulation, fluids, and well-intervention activity (margin and mix impact). ([halliburton.com](https://www.halliburton.com/en/about-us/press-release/halliburton-announces-fourth-quarter-2025-results))

International demand converting into stronger activity levels for directional drilling, unconventionals, well intervention, and artificial lift (revenue stability/upside). ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Sustained capital discipline (capex staying near guided levels) supporting free-cash-flow generation and shareholder returns in a recovering cycle. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))
company_overview: Halliburton provides oilfield services and technology spanning drilling/formation evaluation, well construction and completion, and production optimization across the well lifecycle. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

The company operates two reportable segments: Completion and Production and Drilling and Evaluation, which drive revenue allocation and margin performance. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Strategy emphasizes international growth in directional drilling, unconventionals, well intervention, and artificial lift, while North America focuses on value maximization and electrification/automation platforms. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))
current_context: Q4 2025 results (Jan 21, 2026): revenue of $5.7B, operating margin 13%, adjusted operating margin 15%, operating cash flow $1.2B, and free cash flow $875M; full-year share repurchases were $1B. ([halliburton.com](https://www.halliburton.com/en/about-us/press-release/halliburton-announces-fourth-quarter-2025-results))

FY 2025 context from the latest Form 10-K: total revenue $22.2B (-3% vs. 2024) with total operating income $2.3B including impairments and other charges. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Management reaffirmed capital discipline: 2026 capex guidance of approximately $1.1B (and ~6% of revenue framing). ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case assumes modest 2026-2030 revenue growth with a gradual move toward a normalized EBIT margin (target EBIT margin 0.145 by 2030), consistent with management’s view that international is stable to modestly up while North America remains softer. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Capital intensity remains constrained: forecast capex stays near ~5.6-5.8% of sales, anchored to the company’s expectation of ~6% of revenue and ~$1.1B capex in 2026. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Working-capital intensity is modeled as mean-reverting around ~16.5-16.8% of sales, using the last three fiscal years’ reported balance-sheet working-capital build. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Terminal value anchor (exit EV/EBITDA multiple) is set within the peer range observed in recent oilfield-services comps (mid-cycle multiple for a mature, cyclical services business). ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))
key_risks: Customer E&P capex reductions or commodity-driven downturn causing volume declines and pricing pressure across services. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Margin volatility from impairments/one-time items and system/process transitions (affecting reported operating income versus normalized profitability). ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))

Higher-than-assumed cost of capital (WACC) or weaker terminal EBITDA durability lowering terminal value. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

presentation.subtitle: HAL DCF Input Package (Base/Bull/Bear) — Recovery + Margin Normalization
valuation_summary: DCF base-case uses WACC 0.092, terminal growth 0.020, and an average terminal approach combining a Gordon-growth framework with a terminal EV/EBITDA anchor of 8.0x, aiming to reflect long-run service-cycle economics. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

The comp set shows EV/NTM EBITDA clustering roughly in the mid-single-digit to low-teens range and forward P/E spanning low-teens to low-20s, supporting a valuation framework that is sensitive to cycle and margins. ([mergersandacquisitions.net](https://mergersandacquisitions.net/insights/oil-gas-services-m-a-trends-analysis-report))

Bull/bear scenarios change only what matters most for a cyclical margin story: (i) revenue growth trajectory, (ii) EBIT margin normalization speed/level, and (iii) WACC/terminal valuation inputs. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/733/quartr/annual-report-10-k-52abe-2026-02-06-06-39-49.pdf))
